page: Microsoft Azure F8-2ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It has no local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance scales moderately due to the 2-core limit, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the average category. Memory bandwidth is average, measuring 51.07 GB/sec for large block reads and 34.54 GB/sec for large block writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

The F8-2ams_v7 offers a distinct resource profile, pairing a high-frequency CPU with a massive memory footprint relative to its core count. This makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, avoiding the need to provision excess vCPUs just to acquire sufficient RAM. However, the lack of local storage and weak multi-threaded performance are notable tradeoffs. It is well-suited for memory-intensive database operations, single-threaded data processing, caching layers like Redis (which achieved 6.96 million SET operations per second in testing), and lightweight text processing.
